newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Jan-May budget gap at 2.31 trln lei.
newsitem.headline: Romania Jan-May budget gap at 2.31 trln lei.

text.p: Romania's state budget deficit narrowed in May as budgetary revenues went up from payments of 1996 profit tax, Finance Ministry data showed on Wednesday.

The data, published in a report of the National Statistics Board, showed the budget deficit had narrowed to 2.31 trillion lei over January-May from 2.43 trillion lei in the the first four months of this year.
State revenues climbed by 3.98 trillion lei in May to 13.98 trillion over January-May, with profit tax revenues rising by 1.4 trillion lei to 3.74 trillion.
Spending was 16.26 trillion lei at end-May, sharply up from 12.4 trillion over January-April, with health and education expenditures taking about 21 percent.

Romania's government is still discussing a revision of the 1997 budget, seeking to preserve the consolidated budget gap at 4.5 percent of gross domestic product to meet promises under accords with the International Monetary Fund.
The consolidated budget includes the state budget, local government budgets, social security budget, supplementary pension funds and various other extra-budgetary funds.

An IMF mission is completing a report after reviewing the country's reform progress in recent months. If favourable, the report will enable Romania to draw the second tranche of $86 million from a $430 million stand-by accord.
Details on the budget revisions were unavailable for the moment but ministers previously said social welfare, health and education would be considered priorities.
The revised budget should include changes in inflation and other macro-economic indicators as well as promises of wage indexation and fiscal relaxation.
Under the current 1997 budget -- agreed with the IMF -- the state budget gap was forecast at 12.6 trillion lei, or 5.4 percent of GDP.
It also set year-on-year inflation at 90 percent, but that target is now out of reach after price liberalisation pushed consumer prices 101.2 percent up in June from December 1996. ($=7,434 lei)
